cmeSourceFinding.verdict: A machine-readable contract-spec feed EXISTS and is used. Not a scrape.
cmeSourceFinding.access: anonymous FTP login on port 21 succeeds; files regenerated daily; undated filenames are the current snapshot
cmeSourceFinding.record: FIXML/Batch/SecDef/Instrmt — Desc, Mult, UOM, UOMQty, PxUOM, PxUOMQty, SettlMeth, MinPxIncr, PxQteCcy, ProdCmplx, CFI, Exch, plus per-market <TickRules>
rejected_alternatives: www.cmegroup.com (contract-spec pages and the CmeWS endpoints behind them) — returns HTTP 403 to every non-browser client INCLUDING a plain fetch of /robots.txt. Bot-protected, rendered HTML. Rejected: reading it would mean defeating that protection and presenting a scrape as a feed.

CME Reference Data API v3 — the exchange's documented real-time reference-data product. Requires a registered OAuth API ID created in the CME Customer Center. No anonymous path. Recorded in the catalog as status not-used; adopting it is a credential decision, not a build.
datamine.cmegroup.com — TCP connect fails from this environment; not investigated further since FPRF answered the question.
cmeSourceFinding.why_a_snapshot_rather_than_a_request_pat: The NYMEX futures file alone is ~60MB. scripts/refresh_cme_contract_specs.py materialises a bounded snapshot carrying, per root, the source file, its BizDt, byte length, SHA-256, the contract month the values were read from, and the count of listed months checked for divergent terms. Values are copied verbatim; none are hand-typed or re-derived.
cmeSourceFinding.reproducibility_check: python scripts/refresh_cme_contract_specs.py --check re-pulled all four files and reported 'OK: 11 roots match the committed snapshot', exit 0.
cmeSourceFinding.caveat_recorded_in_the_data: MinPxIncr on the Instrmt element is in the feed's own price convention and is NOT the tick for every product (GC carries MinPxIncr=1 while TickRules gives TickIncr=0.1). Both are carried verbatim so nothing downstream has to guess; a test pins this.

cftcSourceFinding.verdict: CFTC covers all eleven roots. Coverage was never the problem; the KEY was. Four live defects found and fixed.
cftcSourceFinding.key_change: Resolution moved from contract_market_name LIKE '%pattern%' to cftc_contract_market_code, the CFTC's own stable per-market identifier. A code is unique and is not renamed; a name is neither.
defects_found_on_main: /CL matched CRUDE OIL, LIGHT SWEET-WTI (067411), which is ICE FUTURES EUROPE. The NYMEX contract is listed by CFTC as WTI-PHYSICAL (067651). The panel was serving another exchange's book as /CL positioning — a silent substitution.
/ZB matched U.S. TREASURY BONDS (020631) on the DEFUNCT MidAmerica Commodity Exchange, most recent report 2000-05-02. Twenty-six-year-old data was being served as current positioning.
/ZN and /ZT matched NO rows at all. CFTC renamed those markets to UST 10Y NOTE (043602) and UST 2Y NOTE (042601).
/M6E matched EURO FX/BRITISH POUND XRATE (299741), a cross-rate, because a LIKE returns whatever sorts first among several same-date matches. The intended market is EURO FX (099741).
/M6B and /M6A had no mapping at all (the M-prefix strip produced 6B/6A, which were not keys).
/NQ matched nothing — the pattern was NASDAQ-100 STOCK INDEX (MINI); the live market is NASDAQ MINI (209742).
/GC matched both GOLD (088691) and MICRO GOLD (088695); which one won depended on undefined ordering among same-date rows.
cftcSourceFinding.micro_contract_finding: CFTC publishes separate COT series for the INDEX and CRYPTO micros (MICRO E-MINI S&P 500 13874U, MICRO E-MINI NASDAQ-100 209747, MICRO E-MINI RUSSELL 2000 239747, MICRO GOLD 088695, MICRO BITCOIN 133742, MICRO ETHER 146022) — those resolve exactly. It publishes NONE for the micro FX (M6E/M6B/M6A/M6J/M6C), micro energy (MCL) or micro silver/copper (SIL/MHG). Those eight read the full-size parent and are marked parent-contract-proxy with proxy_of and a proxy_note; the adaptive panel surfaces it in the source line.
cftcSourceFinding.publication_schedule: Weekly. Positions as of Tuesday close, published Friday 15:30 ET. Latest report observed 2026-08-11 (a Tuesday), 60 weeks of history available per market.
cftcSourceFinding.credential: COCKPIT_CFTC_APP_TOKEN raises the Socrata rate limit but is not required; every probe in this session ran anonymously.
cftcSourceFinding.collateral_fix: Every symbol in routers/intelligence._FLOW_COMPLEX (the capital-flows panel: /CL /NG /RB /HO /GC /SI /HG /PL /ZC /ZS /ZW /ZL /ES /NQ /ZN /ZB /ZT) now maps. A test asserts the set is fully covered so a future addition cannot silently render a blank row.

linkageDesign.shape: futures_catalog.json mirrors econ_catalog.json: a hand-curated, versioned pointer file where the provider fetches live from the named authority rather than the repo carrying values. Three layers per root, keyed to the AUTHORITY rather than the asset class, which is the abstraction the build scope adopts for non-issuer instruments.

layers.contract_spec: CME FPRF — the contract's own terms. transform=record, units='contract terms'.
layers.cot: CFTC Commitments of Traders — aggregate positioning. transform=net_position, units=contracts. The catalog row is the POINTER (dataset, cftc_contract_market_code, long/short field names); providers/cftc.py fetches the observations against exactly that pointer.
layers.drivers: FRED and EIA — the macro leg. Rows carry the econ_catalog transform vocabulary plus role and provenance class.

linkageDesign.resolution_api: futures_reference.resolve(symbol) returns all three layers; contract_spec(), cot_series(), drivers() return one each; coverage() is the row's own pass/fail instrument (11 roots x 3 layers).
linkageDesign.typed_absence: Every resolution returns verdict present | absent-verified | lookup-failed with the scope searched. An uncovered symbol resolves to three absent-verified layers naming the catalog scope. A missing snapshot record is lookup-failed, never absent-verified, because the lookup did not run.
linkageDesign.no_silent_substitution: resolution is 'exact' or 'parent-contract-proxy'. Proxies carry proxy_of and proxy_note through the provider dict and into the panel's source line. A test asserts non-proxy roots carry no proxy claim, and another asserts two roots cannot claim the same CFTC market exactly.
linkageDesign.provenance_class_on_drivers: verified-live means the series was fetched and confirmed in this session (18 rows, all FRED, confirmed via the keyless fredgraph.csv path: DFII10 DTWEXBGS DGS2 DGS10 DGS30 T10YIE DEXUSEU DEXUSUK DEXUSAL DHHNGSP GASREGW). carried-from-code means the identifier was hoisted out of an existing shipped mapping in app/providers/eia.py and NOT re-verified here (6 rows, all EIA — no EIA key was exercised in this session).
linkageDesign.cot_only_markets: 21 further roots outside the eleven-instrument cohort (HO HG PL ZC ZS ZW ZL MGC ES NQ RTY MES MNQ M2K MBT MET M6J M6C MCL SIL MHG) carry a COT pointer so providers/cftc.py has ONE lookup table instead of a second hand-kept dict. They carry no contract-spec snapshot; the FPRF extraction reads instruments[] only.

remaining: TW-10 owns the depth pass: prove each EIA series non-proxy per symbol for /CL and /NG and wire Treasury issuance for /ZB /ZN /ZT. The six carried-from-code driver rows are the ones that need live verification there.

ng_storage carries series_id '/natural-gas/stor/wkly' — an API path, not a series code, because app/providers/eia.py issues that route with no facet. Giving it a proper EIA series code is TW-10 work; recorded in the row's blurb rather than papered over.

The eleven roots do not yet have an endpoint. futures_reference is import-ready but unexposed; the twin read contract (TW-2) and the agent door (TW-19/TW-20) own the serving surface, and the dispatch scoped this to the cockpit backend.

The FX driver rows m6e/m6b/m6a_rate_diff_proxy carry only the US leg of the rate differential (DGS10). The foreign leg is not in the catalog and the row blurbs say so explicitly. Completing them means adding ECB/BoE/RBA policy or benchmark series.
cme_contract_specs.json will drift as CME relists. The refresh script's --check mode detects it and exits 1; nothing schedules that today.

Mini grain roots XC / XK / XW remain unmapped. They never resolved on main either (the X-prefix strip produced C/K/W, which were not keys). Left as an honest absence rather than mapped on a guess about product identity.

The CFTC Traders in Financial Futures report (asset manager vs leveraged funds) would give a sharper speculative split for the rates and FX roots than legacy non-commercial. Named in the catalog's dataset blurb as a call not made here.
